headline: MinerU’s MCP-enabled document pipeline creates the main interaction risk; prompt-injection and leakage are limited by awesome-selfhosted’s non-runnable, read-only profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-selfhosted is a non-runnable knowledge-management list with no I/O surfaces, so it cannot itself ingest MinerU output. MinerU can expose an MCP server and processes document content, but the pair lacks a documented shared channel or automatic handoff. Any injection would require unusual manual bridging, so blast radius is small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies MinerU output into a prompt consumed by another agent, injection becomes possible.
IF MinerU is connected to a shared MCP or clipboard bridge, attacker-controlled document text can influence downstream instructions.
mitigations: Disable any shared clipboard or paste automation.
Keep MinerU outputs in plain-text review mode only.
Require human review before reusing extracted text as instructions.
Separate the two agents into different sessions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to MinerU outputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-selfhosted touches no data classes and has no filesystem or network egress, while MinerU processes local documents and can call APIs with allowlisted egress. There is no evidence of a shared workspace or sensitive-data flow between them, so leakage is limited to operator-mediated transfer rather than default pair behavior.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive documents into MinerU and then exports them into another system, leakage can occur.
IF MinerU’s allowlisted egress includes a third-party endpoint for extracted content, document text may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Keep sensitive documents out of MinerU unless necessary.
Review MinerU egress allowlist before processing.
Use separate storage locations for inputs and outputs.
Delete exported artifacts after review.
requires-engineering: enforce per-document redaction before export.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-selfhosted has no write, shell, or git capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. MinerU also lacks filesystem write and git modification, though it supports multi-threaded concurrent inference and multiple instances. The pair therefore has little direct write-conflict surface; only operator-shared resources could collide.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external mutable resource through an operator workflow, contention can occur.
IF MinerU instances are run concurrently against the same output directory, race conditions may appear in surrounding tooling.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Run only one MinerU instance per workspace.
Avoid using shared git working trees.
Serialize operator actions between agents.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared downstream resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text, tables, and OCR that can be treated as authoritative downstream, while awesome-selfhosted is a curated knowledge list that may be used as a source of facts or recommendations. The pair can therefore cascade extraction or curation errors into later decisions if outputs are reused without verification, even though no direct action-taking authority is shown.
conditions: IF MinerU output is copied into a downstream workflow without verification, extraction errors can propagate.
IF awesome-selfhosted entries are treated as authoritative facts rather than a directory, downstream decisions may be misled.
mitigations: Verify extracted fields against source documents.
Treat awesome-selfhosted as a directory, not ground truth.
Require human review before acting on extracted data.
Keep provenance metadata with outputs.
requires-engineering: add validation checks between extraction and consumption.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. awesome-selfhosted is a static open-source list with no data handling, while MinerU is a document processor with local inputs and allowlisted egress. The only plausible compliance issue is operator-chosen sensitive document processing, so the pair itself does not establish a default breach.
conditions: IF the operator feeds regulated data into MinerU and exports results to a non-compliant destination, a policy breach can occur.
IF a deployment adds retention or residency constraints outside these profiles, compliance risk increases.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data unless policy is confirmed.
Check retention settings before processing.
Restrict exports to approved destinations.
Delete temporary outputs promptly.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls.
